prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (policy commitments only)

- Economy and tax: Run a budget surplus and reduce debt; raise the personal allowance to £12,500 and the higher-rate threshold to £50,000; no rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance rates; tackle tax evasion/avoidance; support regional growth (e.g., “Northern Powerhouse”) and city devolution with elected mayors.

- Finance and markets: Complete bank ring‑fencing by 2019; maintain a bank levy; strengthen consumer protection; foster challenger banks and financial technology; extend Funding for Lending; launch “Help to Grow” to close the scale‑up finance gap; boost international tax transparency.

- Infrastructure and digital: Invest over £100bn, including £38bn for rail (HS2/HS3, electrification, Crossrail), £15bn for roads, freeze regulated commuter rail fares in real terms, expand cycling; deliver superfast broadband to 95% by end‑2017, pursue ultrafast coverage, improve mobile to 90% landmass and lead on 5G.

- Jobs, business and skills: Create 2m jobs; deliver 3m apprenticeships; abolish employers’ NICs for young apprentices; review business rates; cut £10bn of red tape; expand Start Up Loans and SME public procurement; permanent Office of Tax Simplification; boost exports.

- Work and fairness: Publish gender pay gap data for large employers; aim to halve the disability employment gap; enforce the Minimum Wage; ban exclusivity in zero‑hours contracts.

- Education and training: Tougher primary standards and resits; promote core GCSEs (English, maths, science, language, history/geography); convert failing/coasting schools to academies; open at least 500 free schools; protect per‑pupil funding and pupil premium; recruit more maths/physics teachers; expand University Technical Colleges and degree apprenticeships; remove the cap on university places; introduce postgraduate loans; strengthen special educational needs support; protect children online.

- Welfare and immigration: Roll out Universal Credit; lower the household benefit cap to £23,000 and freeze most working‑age benefits for two years (with exemptions); link the personal allowance to the Minimum Wage (“Tax‑Free Minimum Wage”); reform EU migrant access to in‑work benefits and social housing; tighten enforcement (exit checks, landlord status checks, “deport first, appeal later”); expand action on modern slavery; require fluent English for public‑facing workers.

- Health and care: Increase NHS spending by at least £8bn above inflation by 2020; provide 7‑day GP/hospital services and same‑day GP appointments for over‑75s; expand online access and electronic health records (with opt‑out); strengthen mental health access standards; pursue cancer and dementia strategies; national diabetes prevention; integrate health and social care and cap residential care costs.

- Housing and planning: Extend Help to Buy and launch a Help to Buy ISA; build 200,000 discounted Starter Homes for under‑40s and 275,000 additional affordable homes; extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants with replacements; prioritise brownfield (registers and permissions) and protect the Green Belt; support garden towns; enable self/custom build.

- Environment and energy: Create a UK “Blue Belt” of marine protections; plant 11m trees; improve air/water quality and flood defences; expand pocket parks; promote competition and smart meters by 2020; insulate 1m homes; support nuclear, CCS, shale and North Sea investment; end new subsidies for onshore wind and give communities final say; meet climate targets cost‑effectively.

- Crime, justice and extremism: Continue police reform and technology adoption; strengthen cyber capability; overhaul complaints and stop‑and‑search performance; ban new psychoactive substances; modernise prisons; enact a Victims’ Law; tackle violence against women and girls; extend the Unduly Lenient Scheme; introduce a British Bill of Rights and new communications data powers; create banning and disruption orders against extremist groups/individuals; tighten rules on extremist speakers and employment with children.

- Older people and savings: Maintain the State Pension triple lock; introduce the single‑tier pension; keep key pensioner benefits; extend pension freedoms and tax‑free inheritance of pension pots; raise the effective inheritance tax threshold for the family home to £1m for couples; cap care costs and allow deferred payments.

- Governance, Union, EU, and foreign policy: Cut government waste; expand digital public services and transparency; implement English votes for English laws; reform boundaries and reduce MPs to 600; devolve further powers to Scotland and Wales; implement the Stormont House Agreement; hold an in‑out EU referendum by end‑2017; protect non‑euro members’ interests, pursue Single Market reform and trade deals; maintain Armed Forces (Army ≥82,000), renew the nuclear deterrent, invest in equipment and cyber; meet the 0.7% aid target focused on health, education, water/sanitation, crisis response, and women/girls.
